206	    /// The clips keep their relative times — the earliest starts at 0 inside
207	    /// the nest — their relative track order, their props and their actions;
208	    /// the nest clip covers exactly the span they covered, on the front-most
209	    /// track any of them was on.
210	    ///
211	    /// An empty selection, and a selection of one clip that is already a
212	    /// nest (grouping a group alone changes nothing a user can see), are
213	    /// identities. A nest clip that would break the overlap rule against
214	    /// whatever was NOT selected is refused, in the rule's own sentence. `Err` on an unknown clip id or a selection
215	    /// that would put the project past the track cap.
216	    pub fn nest_clips(&self, clips: &[u32], name: Option<&str>) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
217	        // A linked partner goes in with its clip (spec §11 AU-91).
218	        let selected: Vec<Clip> = self
219	            .selected_clips(&self.with_links(clips)?)?
220	            .into_iter()
221	            .cloned()
222	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
223	        if selected.is_empty() {
224	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
225	        }
226	        if selected.len() == 1 && matches!(selected[0].source, Source::Nest { .. }) {
227	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
228	        }
229	        // An adjustment clip grades the top level only (spec §11 GR-6).
230	        if let Some(found) = selected.iter().find(|c| is_adjustment(c)) {
231	            return Ok(Outcome::Refused(adjustment_cannot_nest(found.id)));
232	        }
233	
234	        let earliest = selected.iter().map(|c| c.start).min().unwrap_or(0);
235	        let latest = selected.iter().map(clip_end).max().unwrap_or(0);
236	        if latest <= earliest {
237	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
238	        }
239	
240	        // The source tracks, back-most first, so the nest's own stack keeps
241	        // the order the timeline had. `track_index` is the stack position;
242	        // a clip on a track that is not in `tracks` cannot exist (`validate`
243	        // refuses it) and is skipped rather than defended against twice.
244	        let mut sources: Vec<(usize, u32)> = Vec::new();
245	        for clip in &selected {
246	            if let Some(index) = self.track_index(clip.track) {
247	                if !sources.iter().any(|(_, id)| *id == clip.track) {
248	                    sources.push((index, clip.track));
249	                }
250	            }
251	        }
252	        sources.sort_unstable();
253	        // The front-most source track that is not a matte track is where
254	        // the nest clip goes (MT-5): a matte pair nested together must land
255	        // where its picture was drawn, not on the matte track, where the
256	        // whole nest would become a matte. The front-most when all are. The
257	        // nest's own tracks count toward `MAX_TRACKS` like any other
258	        // (`format::check_caps`), so a selection that would overrun the cap
259	        // is caught by `finish` rather than counted twice here.
260	        let drawn = sources
261	            .iter()
262	            .rev()
263	            .find(|(_, id)| self.track(*id).is_some_and(|t| t.matte.is_none()));
264	        let Some((_, front_track)) = drawn.or(sources.last()).copied() else {
265	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
266	        };
267	
268	        let mut next = self.clone();
269	        let nest_id = next.allocate_id();
270	        let mut tracks: Vec<Track> = Vec::with_capacity(sources.len());
271	        let mut mapping: Vec<(u32, u32)> = Vec::with_capacity(sources.len());
272	        for (_, id) in &sources {
273	            let Some(source) = self.track(*id) else {
274	                continue;
275	            };
276	            let track = nested_track(&mut next, source, *id != front_track);
277	            mapping.push((*id, track.id));
278	            tracks.push(track);
279	        }
280	        // The carry rule (MT-5), one pass over the mapping: a nested track
281	        // stays a matte only when the nested track directly behind it is the
282	        // copy of its source's target. A matte nested without its target
283	    /// Each clip returns at `clip.start + its own start`, with fresh ids, on
284	    /// the track counted back from the nest clip's own: the nest's
285	    /// front-most NON-matte track (the front-most when all are, MT-5) lands
286	    /// where the nest clip was, the one behind it a track further back, a
287	    /// carried matte track in front of it a track further forward, and
288	    /// tracks missing behind are added. A clip the overlap rule refuses —
289	    /// or a matte clip with no track in front — goes on a new track in
290	    /// front, ordinary: `unnest` makes no track a matte.
291	    ///
292	    /// The nest itself is dropped when nothing else shows it; a second clip
293	    /// showing it keeps it, which is why the returned clips are copies.
294	    /// `Err` when `clip` is not a nest clip.
295	    pub fn unnest_clip(&self, clip: u32) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
296	        let target = self.require_clip(clip)?.clone();
297	        let Source::Nest { project } = target.source else {
298	            return Err(format!("clip {clip} is not a nest clip"));
299	        };
300	        // `validate` refuses a clip pointing at a nest that is not there, so
301	        // this is a corrupt project rather than a caller's mistake — an
302	        // error either way, naming both ids.
303	        let nest = self
304	            .nest(project)
305	            .ok_or_else(|| format!("clip {clip} shows unknown nest {project}"))?
306	            .clone();
307	
308	        let base = self.require_track_index(target.track)? as i64;
309	        // The nest's front-most non-matte track, the one the nest clip's own
310	        // track stands for (MT-5); the front-most when all are mattes.
311	        let front = nest
312	            .tracks
313	            .iter()
314	            .rposition(|t| t.matte.is_none())
315	            .unwrap_or(nest.tracks.len().saturating_sub(1)) as i64;
316	        let depth = |track: u32| -> i64 {
317	            // 0 for `front`, counting backwards; negative for a carried
318	            // matte track in front of it.
319	            match nest.tracks.iter().position(|t| t.id == track) {
320	                Some(index) => front - index as i64,
321	                None => 0,
322	            }
323	        };
324	        // Bounded by the track cap the project was read under, so the
325	        // deficit loop below can ask for at most `MAX_TRACKS` tracks and
326	        // `finish` refuses the result if that is too many.
327	        let deepest = front;
328	
329	        let mut next = self.clone();
330	        next.clips.retain(|c| c.id != clip);
331	
332	        // Tracks missing behind the destination, exactly as `paste` adds
333	        // them: inserting at index 0 shifts every existing track up, so the
334	        // destination index moves with them.
335	        let base = next.add_tracks_behind(deepest, base);
336	
337	        // Back-most first, then time: the order clips are placed in is the
338	        // order the overlap rule sees them, so it has to be deterministic or
339	        // one nest could open two ways.
340	        let mut ordered: Vec<&Clip> = nest.clips.iter().collect();
341	        ordered.sort_by_key(|c| (std::cmp::Reverse(depth(c.track)), c.start, c.id));
342	
343	        let mut landing = Landing::new(base);
344	        let first = next.clips.len();
345	        let mut fresh: HashMap<u32, u32> = HashMap::new();
346	        for source in ordered {
347	            let mut moved = source.clone();
348	            next.remint(&mut moved);
349	            fresh.insert(source.id, moved.id);
350	            // Translate first; the shared normalization then handles a
351	            // hand-written or legacy off-grid nest on the parent grid.
352	            moved.start = target.start.saturating_add(source.start);
353	            next.resnap_clip_times(&mut moved);
354	            landing.land(&mut next, moved, depth(source.track));
355	        }
356	        // The returning clips re-pair through their fresh ids (AU-96).
357	        if let Some(landed) = next.clips.get_mut(first..) {
358	            relink_copies(landed, &fresh);
359	        }
360	
361	        if !next.nest_is_shown(project) {
362	            next.nests.retain(|n| n.id != project);
363	        }
364	        self.finish_placement(next, landing.touched())
365	    }
366	}

539	//! The transitions a layer plays at one instant (spec §7.3, §11 MT-8): each
540	//! recipe layer's `transition` and `dissolve`.
541	//!
542	//! A layer inside `n` nest clips has `n + 1` LEVELS, walked inner to outer:
543	//! its own clip in the innermost container, then each enclosing nest clip in
544	//! ITS container, outward to the timeline. Each level asks
545	//! [`transition::transition_among`] — the one transition lookup — at that
546	//! container's own time.
547	//!
548	//! ### Routed and unrouted
549	//!
550	//! A `cross_dissolve` or `zoom` whose container is a nest, or one of whose
551	//! two clips is a nest clip, is ROUTED ([`routed`], the one predicate): the
552	//! compositor draws each half alone into a target of its own and mixes the
553	//! two (§7.5), because a half that is more than one layer — or a layer that
554	//! is not on the canvas, a nest clip — cannot carry the per-layer weight
555	//! correction a timeline pair does (MT-3). A routed level is an entry in the
556	//! layer's `dissolve`, never its `transition`; `transition` is the innermost
557	//! level's answer that is NOT routed, as `recipe.rs`'s `transition_of`
558	//! answered every kind before issue batch B90 moved its walk here. A push,
559	//! slide, wipe or fade is never routed: none applies a partner correction.
560	//!
561	//! ### The contract the compositor relies on
562	//!
563	//! `dissolve` is `null` or the routed levels, OUTERMOST first, each
564	//! `{id, kind, role, progress, anchor}`. A dissolve is one [`DissolveKey`]:
565	//! the nest clips enclosing its container, its earlier clip and its later
566	//! clip, so two clips showing one nest at one instant each have their own.
567	//! Ids are dense from 0 in first-seen order, walking layers back to front,
568	//! each chain outermost first. `anchor` is the canvas point (top-left frame)
569	//! the half is placed at: the layer's own anchor at its own level, the
570	//! centre of the nest's placed canvas rectangle at a nest clip's. A layer
571	//! drawn into a matte keeps only the routed levels at or inside its first
572	//! matte level — the matte is drawn whole, and the half it lies in fades it
573	//! once — while its `transition` is still sought outward.

1	# Spec §11 — decisions: Mattes (#240, road map "mattes")
2	
3	Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
4	[`README.md`](README.md).
5	
6	The road map that made these is closed: its condensed record is `designs/adr/mattes.md`, and the
7	original, `archive/mattes.md`, holds each phase's record (MT0–MT5). MT-1..MT-6 were recorded in
8	MT0, before any code, and MT-6's choice of route was filled from MT0's spike
9	(`tools/proof/matte_spike/`); MT-7 (the chrome) was recorded at MT4's start, before its code.
10	They are not G- decisions: a matte is a track relation the compositor draws for any clip, not a
11	graphics decision (road map 10's own plan: "Mattes are compositor features",
12	`designs/adr/svg-motion-plan.md`). The video-input half of #240 is #251, and nothing here decides
13	it.
14	
15	- **MT-1 — A matte is a track relation in a closed vocabulary, drawn by the one compositor; R5-1
16	  and G-1 stand.** A track's `matte` is `none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or
17	  `luma_inverted`, set by `set_track {matte}` (`none` switches it off). A matte track's clips are
18	  never drawn on the canvas; at each instant what they show cuts every layer the track directly
19	  behind draws (MT-2). Any clip that draws can be one — text, shape, image, graphic, video, nest.
20	  Nothing is a package, a shader or an expression, and a graphic on a matte track is called with
21	  the same arguments and keyed the same way as anywhere (G-5, G-9 untouched). A clip is a matte
22	  only by the track it is on: moved off, it is ordinary; the tracks `paste` adds are ordinary;
23	  `duplicate` keeps its track. Persisted as `tracks[].matte`, written only when not `none` — the
24	  model's first `skip_serializing_if`, so every older file and every ordinary track round-trips
25	  byte for byte and the reader's default is the same answer. `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` 14, no migrate
26	  step. The video half of #240 is #251 and nothing here decides it.
27	  **Amended (CO5, spec §11 CO-50):** a matte group can also be a clip's SUBJECT: drawn by a copy
28	  of a cut-out layer, never by a track; only a track makes a clip a matte.
29	- **MT-2 — What a matte cuts, and when it cuts nothing.** Its target is the track directly behind
30	  it in its own container (the timeline, or one nest's own tracks) when that track is not itself
31	  a matte track. With no such track (the back-most track, or a matte behind it) a matte cuts
32	  nothing and its clips still draw nothing. Where the matte track shows nothing at an instant — no
33	  clip, the track hidden, a clip's video off — the track behind shows uncut (owner, 2026-10-07,
34	  choice 5). Read per instant and per pair of tracks: no clip names another, so split, move,
35	  delete, paste, nest and undo cannot break a link; `add_track`, `move_track` and `remove_track`
36	  change which track is behind, visibly. A matte track's clips sound as on any track, and Mute
37	  Audio silences them (owner, 2026-10-08, O1): a matte is a picture rule, like Hide Video.
38	  **Amended (CO5, spec §11 CO-50):** a clip with `video.behind_subject` is cut by the subjects
39	  behind it as well as by any matte in front of its track; the cuts multiply.
40	- **MT-3 — The four modes, and where the cut is applied.** At a pixel the matte's composite —
41	  premultiplied, in encoded sRGB like every stage of the compositor (§7.5) — gives: `alpha` its
42	  alpha a; `alpha_inverted` 1 − a; `luma` the Rec. 709 luma (0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722, the weights
43	  the shader's saturation uses) of its premultiplied colour, so transparent counts as black;
44	  `luma_inverted` 1 − that. The value multiplies the matted layer's coverage at the fragment
45	  stage's step 7, beside the corner radius and the nest clip rectangle, sampled at the fragment's
46	  own canvas position. So the matted clip's own drop shadow follows the cut-out shape (its

182	//! `nest` and `unnest` — grouping (spec §6, table "Clips").
183	//!
184	//! The two halves of one idea: a selection of clips becomes ONE clip on the
185	//! timeline showing a [`Nest`], and a nest clip becomes the clips again.
186	//! Their own module because grouping is a different concern from placement
187	//! — no other op changes which CONTAINER a clip lives in — and because the
188	//! pair only makes sense read together.
189	//!
190	//! ### They are inverses, up to ids
191	//!
192	//! `nest` then `unnest` gives back the clips it took: same sources, same
193	//! relative times, same props, same actions, same stacking. The ids differ,
194	//! exactly as they do across `split` then a re-join, because `unnest` mints
195	//! fresh ones — it has to, since a second clip may still show the same nest
196	//! and the clips inside it cannot be in two places at once.
197	//!
198	//! Two asymmetries are deliberate, and both come from the schema:
199	//!
200	//! - **A trimmed nest clip gives everything back.** `Source::Nest` has no in
201	//!   point (spec §5.2), so `unnest` is the inverse of `nest`, not of the
202	
203	impl Project {
204	    /// Collapses `clips` into one nest clip (spec §6).
205	    ///
206	    /// The clips keep their relative times — the earliest starts at 0 inside
207	    /// the nest — their relative track order, their props and their actions;
208	    /// the nest clip covers exactly the span they covered, on the front-most
209	    /// track any of them was on.
210	    ///
211	    /// An empty selection, and a selection of one clip that is already a
212	    /// nest (grouping a group alone changes nothing a user can see), are
213	    /// identities. A nest clip that would break the overlap rule against
214	    /// whatever was NOT selected is refused, in the rule's own sentence. `Err` on an unknown clip id or a selection
215	    /// that would put the project past the track cap.
216	    pub fn nest_clips(&self, clips: &[u32], name: Option<&str>) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
217	        // A linked partner goes in with its clip (spec §11 AU-91).
218	        let selected: Vec<Clip> = self
219	            .selected_clips(&self.with_links(clips)?)?
220	            .into_iter()
221	            .cloned()
222	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
223	        if selected.is_empty() {
224	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
225	        }
226	        if selected.len() == 1 && matches!(selected[0].source, Source::Nest { .. }) {
227	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
228	        }
229	        // An adjustment clip grades the top level only (spec §11 GR-6).
230	        if let Some(found) = selected.iter().find(|c| is_adjustment(c)) {
231	            return Ok(Outcome::Refused(adjustment_cannot_nest(found.id)));
232	        }
233	
234	        let earliest = selected.iter().map(|c| c.start).min().unwrap_or(0);
235	        let latest = selected.iter().map(clip_end).max().unwrap_or(0);
236	        if latest <= earliest {
237	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
238	        }
239	
240	        // The source tracks, back-most first, so the nest's own stack keeps
241	        // the order the timeline had. `track_index` is the stack position;
242	        // a clip on a track that is not in `tracks` cannot exist (`validate`
243	        // refuses it) and is skipped rather than defended against twice.
244	        let mut sources: Vec<(usize, u32)> = Vec::new();
245	        for clip in &selected {
246	            if let Some(index) = self.track_index(clip.track) {
247	                if !sources.iter().any(|(_, id)| *id == clip.track) {
248	                    sources.push((index, clip.track));
249	                }
250	            }
251	        }
252	        sources.sort_unstable();
253	        // The front-most source track that is not a matte track is where
254	        // the nest clip goes (MT-5): a matte pair nested together must land
255	        // where its picture was drawn, not on the matte track, where the
256	        // whole nest would become a matte. The front-most when all are. The
257	        // nest's own tracks count toward `MAX_TRACKS` like any other
258	        // (`format::check_caps`), so a selection that would overrun the cap
259	        // is caught by `finish` rather than counted twice here.
260	        let drawn = sources
261	            .iter()
262	            .rev()
263	            .find(|(_, id)| self.track(*id).is_some_and(|t| t.matte.is_none()));
264	        let Some((_, front_track)) = drawn.or(sources.last()).copied() else {
265	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
266	        };
267	
268	        let mut next = self.clone();
269	        let nest_id = next.allocate_id();
270	        let mut tracks: Vec<Track> = Vec::with_capacity(sources.len());
271	        let mut mapping: Vec<(u32, u32)> = Vec::with_capacity(sources.len());
272	        for (_, id) in &sources {
273	            let Some(source) = self.track(*id) else {
274	                continue;
275	            };
276	            let track = nested_track(&mut next, source, *id != front_track);
277	            mapping.push((*id, track.id));
278	            tracks.push(track);
279	        }
280	        // The carry rule (MT-5), one pass over the mapping: a nested track
281	        // stays a matte only when the nested track directly behind it is the
282	        // copy of its source's target. A matte nested without its target
283	    /// Each clip returns at `clip.start + its own start`, with fresh ids, on
284	    /// the track counted back from the nest clip's own: the nest's
285	    /// front-most NON-matte track (the front-most when all are, MT-5) lands
286	    /// where the nest clip was, the one behind it a track further back, a
287	    /// carried matte track in front of it a track further forward, and
288	    /// tracks missing behind are added. A clip the overlap rule refuses —
289	    /// or a matte clip with no track in front — goes on a new track in
290	    /// front, ordinary: `unnest` makes no track a matte.
291	    ///
292	    /// The nest itself is dropped when nothing else shows it; a second clip
293	    /// showing it keeps it, which is why the returned clips are copies.
294	    /// `Err` when `clip` is not a nest clip.
295	    pub fn unnest_clip(&self, clip: u32) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
296	        let target = self.require_clip(clip)?.clone();
297	        let Source::Nest { project } = target.source else {
298	            return Err(format!("clip {clip} is not a nest clip"));
299	        };
300	        // `validate` refuses a clip pointing at a nest that is not there, so
301	        // this is a corrupt project rather than a caller's mistake — an
302	        // error either way, naming both ids.
303	        let nest = self
304	            .nest(project)
305	            .ok_or_else(|| format!("clip {clip} shows unknown nest {project}"))?
306	            .clone();
307	
308	        let base = self.require_track_index(target.track)? as i64;
309	        // The nest's front-most non-matte track, the one the nest clip's own
310	        // track stands for (MT-5); the front-most when all are mattes.
311	        let front = nest
312	            .tracks
313	            .iter()
314	            .rposition(|t| t.matte.is_none())
315	            .unwrap_or(nest.tracks.len().saturating_sub(1)) as i64;
316	        let depth = |track: u32| -> i64 {
317	            // 0 for `front`, counting backwards; negative for a carried
318	            // matte track in front of it.
319	            match nest.tracks.iter().position(|t| t.id == track) {
320	                Some(index) => front - index as i64,
321	                None => 0,
322	            }
323	        };
324	        // Bounded by the track cap the project was read under, so the
325	        // deficit loop below can ask for at most `MAX_TRACKS` tracks and
326	        // `finish` refuses the result if that is too many.
327	        let deepest = front;
328	
329	        let mut next = self.clone();
330	        next.clips.retain(|c| c.id != clip);
331	
332	        // Tracks missing behind the destination, exactly as `paste` adds
333	        // them: inserting at index 0 shifts every existing track up, so the
334	        // destination index moves with them.
335	        let base = next.add_tracks_behind(deepest, base);
336	
337	        // Back-most first, then time: the order clips are placed in is the
338	        // order the overlap rule sees them, so it has to be deterministic or
339	        // one nest could open two ways.
340	        let mut ordered: Vec<&Clip> = nest.clips.iter().collect();
341	        ordered.sort_by_key(|c| (std::cmp::Reverse(depth(c.track)), c.start, c.id));
342	
343	        let mut landing = Landing::new(base);
344	        let first = next.clips.len();
345	        let mut fresh: HashMap<u32, u32> = HashMap::new();
346	        for source in ordered {
347	            let mut moved = source.clone();
348	            next.remint(&mut moved);
349	            fresh.insert(source.id, moved.id);
350	            // Translate first; the shared normalization then handles a
351	            // hand-written or legacy off-grid nest on the parent grid.
352	            moved.start = target.start.saturating_add(source.start);
353	            next.resnap_clip_times(&mut moved);
354	            landing.land(&mut next, moved, depth(source.track));
355	        }
356	        // The returning clips re-pair through their fresh ids (AU-96).
357	        if let Some(landed) = next.clips.get_mut(first..) {
358	            relink_copies(landed, &fresh);
359	        }
360	
361	        if !next.nest_is_shown(project) {
362	            next.nests.retain(|n| n.id != project);
363	        }
364	        self.finish_placement(next, landing.touched())
365	    }
366	}

add_adjustment_clip Adds an adjustment clip — Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip. It has no picture of its own: while it lasts it grades everything drawn BEHIND it (every lower track and the canvas background, never a track in front) with the colour and the point filters (sepia, noir, vignette, invert) that set_video gives it, and its opacity is the grade's strength. On a track cut by a matte it grades only inside the matte; on a matte track it does nothing. Refused inside a nest and in any transition or overlap — fade it with opacity instead; blur, sharpen, pixelate and a blend mode are errors on it.
{"type": "object", "properties": {"scope": {"type": "integer", "description": "Edit INSIDE a nest, by nest id \u2014 get_project lists them under nests, and a nest clip's source.project names the one it shows. With it, every id in this call \u2014 clips, tracks, actions \u2014 is looked up in THAT nest's own tracks and clips instead of the timeline's, and every time is the nest's own, measured from its zero (a nest has no speed, so the whole mapping is t minus the nest clip's start); media ids are unaffected, because a nest shares the document's media. The op itself is unchanged and one call is still one undo step. Omit it to edit whatever the app has OPEN \u2014 the timeline, or the nest set_scope entered, exactly as an edit made by hand goes where the window is looking \u2014 so this arg

add_background Puts a backdrop on a NEW back-most track, starting at 0 and running the timeline's length — Clip ▸ Add Background. With no arguments at all it is a canvas-sized WHITE rectangle, which is what the menu's Solid Color row sends: white rather than black because the canvas is already black, so a black plate would be a command that appears to do nothing. Give it a color to paint the plate another colour, or a media to put that picture there instead, at FILL scale — where add_clip would Fit it, because a plate that leaves the canvas showing down one side has failed at that. A video or audio plate stops where its file does, an image runs the timeline. A full-canvas GRADIENT is this clip and a set_shape {gradient} after it. media and color are alternatives: both is an error, as is a sub-frame duration or media, or one with no pictures.

It is MUTED — its enabled becomes {video: true, audio: false}, or the mix would play one recording twice — and it drops the original's audio.duck along with its transition, actions and label. The duck goes because it is the one field of that group that lowers OTHER material: a copy keeping it would duck the whole mix, including the clip it was copied from. /// timeline's. They are the same tracks and clips — a nest is a group held
/// in the parent's one id space, and flattening one at evaluation time
/// gives its clips real composition tracks — so counting them separately
/// would let a project with 64 nests of 64 tracks past a cap that exists to
/// bound exactly that.
pub fn check_caps(p: &Project) -> Result<(), String> {
    let nested_clips: usize = p.nests.iter().map(|n| n.clips.len()).sum();
    let nested_tracks: usize = p.nests.iter().map(|n| n.tracks.len()).sum();
    let clips = p.clips.len().saturating_add(nested_clips);
    let tracks = p.tracks.len().saturating_add(nested_tracks);
    if clips > MAX_CLIPS {
        return Err(format!("too many clips: {clips} (max {MAX_CLIPS})"));

---
title: Backgrounds
description: Fill the space around your footage with a colour, a picture or a blurred copy of the clip, on a new track behind everything.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A screen recording that doesn't fill the frame, a phone clip on a landscape canvas or a title standing on nothing all leave the canvas showing. A background fills that space with a colour, a picture or a blurred copy of the clip itself.

To change the colour of the canvas itself, see [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={[
    'Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color',
    'Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image…',
    'Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background',
  ]}
  tools={['add_background', 'add_blurred_background']}
/>

## Solid Color

Choose **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color**. You don't need a selection, and there's no key for it.

Frame Job adds a canvas-sized white rectangle named "Background", starting at 0 and as long as the timeline. It's white because the canvas is black by default, and a black plate would seem to do nothing.

Recolour it in the **Fill** row of the **Shape** tab, or turn on **Gradient** there for a full-canvas ramp. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) and [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/).

## Image

<Steps>

1. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image…**. You don't need a selection, and there's no key for it.

2. Pick a picture. The panel offers any image type macOS can read, and only image files.

</Steps>

The picture goes behind everything, scaled to fill the canvas and as long as the timeline. It's named "Background". Fill means it covers the whole canvas and any overflow is cut off at the edges, whatever **Fit new clips to canvas** says. To see the whole picture instead, scale it down afterwards.

The picture joins the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) in the same undo step. If it's already there, the existing entry is reused.

If the file can't be read, an alert says so and nothing is added. "Could Not Add the Picture" means it couldn't join the project's media list.

## Blurred background

This is the usual backdrop for a screen recording or a vertical video: the clip's own picture, blown up past the frame and blurred, so the colours always match.

<Steps>

1. Select one clip.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**. There's no key for it.

</Steps>

Frame Job puts a copy behind everything, named "Blurred Background", and selects the copy rather than the original, so you can adjust its blur or its scale straight away. The copy is:

- at the same start and length, with the same speed and the same part of the source, so both play the same frames
- scaled to fill the canvas, centred and uncropped
- blended **Normal**, whatever the original uses
- blurred by one full-strength Blur [filter](/effects/filters/), which replaces any filters on the original
- muted, so the sound doesn't play twice

The command works on video, image, still, shape and graphic clips. It's dimmed for a text clip, an adjustment clip and an audio-only clip, which have no picture size to scale to the canvas. It's also dimmed for a nest clip, because a blurred copy of a nest would come out sharp, and when you've selected no clips or more than one.

## What a blurred background follows

The copy matches the clip at the moment you add it. After that it's a separate clip: moving or trimming the original doesn't move or trim the copy.

| The copy leaves behind | So |
| --- | --- |
| Transition | It's alone on its track, with nothing to transition from. |
| Actions | A zoom on the foreground doesn't zoom the backdrop. A speed ramp is an action too, so a copy of a ramped clip plays at the clip's steady speed and doesn't stay in step with it. |
| Motion presets and Motion Blur | The backdrop stays still and draws sharp, before its blur. |
| Remove Background and Behind Subject | The backdrop stays whole. |
| Label and ducking | The label isn't copied, and the copy doesn't lower the rest of the mix. |

Everything else carries over, including opacity, rotation, corner radius, the colour controls, the drop shadow and the reflection. A rotated clip gives a rotated backdrop, and the fill is worked out as if the picture were square to the canvas, so a large rotation can leave the corners showing.

The copy's picture is always on, even if the original's is [turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).

## A new back-most track

Each of the three commands puts one clip on a new track behind every other track, and selects it. A new track is the only place that's sure to be behind everything, with no overlap to check.

The track gets the next numbered name, such as "Track 4". One undo step takes the clip and the track away again. The steps are called **Add Background** and **Add Blurred Background**.

## Good to know

- A plate is as long as the timeline when you add it, and it doesn't grow with the timeline. Drag its end to [trim](/editing/trimming/) it longer.
- On an empty timeline, a plate is one frame long.
- Fill stops at a scale of 1000%, so a source less than a tenth of the canvas's width or height can't reach the edges.
- With a nest open, a background goes on the nest's own tracks, behind everything inside the nest.
- A project holds up to 64 tracks, counting the tracks inside nests, and Frame Job won't add a background past that.

## With an agent

An agent can do two things the menu can't. It can paint the plate in a chosen colour and give it a length of its own, and it can use a movie that's already in the project instead of a picture. A movie plate keeps its sound and stops where its file ends, so only a picture or a colour runs the whole timeline. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).

## Related

- [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/)
- [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/)
- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)

---
title: Matte tracks
description: Make one track cut the track behind it, so text, a shape or a movie becomes a window onto your footage.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A matte track cuts the track directly behind it. Its own clips are never drawn. Instead, what they show decides where the track behind can be seen, which turns a title or a shape into a window onto your footage.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Track ▸ Matte"
  where="Right-click a track's header or the empty part of its lane ▸ Matte"
  tools={['set_track', 'add_adjustment_clip']}
/>

<Shot
  name="10c-matte-track.window"
  alt="The editor with three tracks. The Window track carries a Matte · Alpha tag and its rectangle clip is drawn pale with a bracket joining it to the Video track below, so the preview shows the video only inside the rectangle, on a black canvas. The Stray track in front reads Matte · nothing behind. The inspector's Picture sub-tab opens with the note: Matte for the track below (Alpha). Not drawn: its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect."
/>

## What a matte does

Any clip that draws can be a matte: text, a shape, a graphic, an image, a movie or a nest.

A matte belongs to the track, not the clip. Move a clip off the track and it's an ordinary clip again, and move one on and it becomes part of the matte.

Only the track directly behind is cut, so tracks further back and the canvas show through the hole. Adding, moving or removing a track can change which track that is.

The cut applies to everything the clip behind draws. Its drop shadow follows the cut-out shape, and its reflection is cut where it lands. It all works in the preview, in rendered frames, at every [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/) and in every export.

## Setting a matte

<Steps>

1. Put the clips that will do the cutting on the track directly in front of the track you want to cut.

2. Select one of those clips, or right-click that track's header.

3. Choose a mode from **Track ▸ Matte**, or from the **Matte** submenu of the track's context menu.

</Steps>

**Track ▸ Matte** works on the track holding the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected. The context menu works on the track you clicked. Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click its header or the empty part of its lane to open it.

A checkmark shows the track's mode. Choosing the mode it already has beeps and makes no undo step. There's no key for a matte, and the undo step is called **Track Matte**.

## The modes

| Mode | The track behind shows where the matte clip is |
| --- | --- |
| **Off** | Not a matte. This is an ordinary track, and every track's default. |
| **Alpha** | Opaque |
| **Inverted Alpha** | Transparent |
| **Luma** | Bright |
| **Inverted Luma** | Dark |

Brightness is Rec. 709 luma, and transparent counts as black, so a half-transparent white counts as half bright.

Everything outside a matte clip's box is transparent. So while a matte clip is on the timeline, **Alpha** and **Luma** hide the track behind outside the clip, and **Inverted Alpha** and **Inverted Luma** show it there.

## Gaps

Where the matte track has no clip, the track behind shows uncut, whatever the mode.

A matte is read moment by moment and no clip is tied to another, so splitting, moving, deleting or pasting can't break a link between them.

## Turning a matte off

To turn a cut off for a while, use **Hide Video** on the matte track, or [turn off a matte clip's picture](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/). Either way the track behind shows whole, as it does in a gap. To end the matte for good, choose **Off**.

## Nothing to cut

A matte with no target cuts nothing, and its clips still draw nothing. That happens on the back-most track, and on a track directly in front of another matte track. So two matte tracks in a row don't combine: only the one nearest the track behind cuts anything.

## Matte properties

A matte clip is drawn like any other clip, into the matte instead of onto the canvas, so most of its settings shape the cut:

- position, scale, rotation and crop
- corner radius and opacity
- colour, chroma key and filters
- spotlight and obscured regions
- motion presets and actions
- transitions between two matte clips

Animate the clip and the cut moves with it, so a moving title can wipe footage on.

A matte clip's blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect. They're kept, and apply again when the track stops being a matte.

**Motion Blur** has no effect either, on a matte clip or on a clip a matte is cutting. Both draw sharp.

A matte clip isn't drawn, but it's still there on the canvas. Click inside its box to select it, and drag it like any clip.

## Sound

A matte clip's sound still plays. A matte only changes the picture, so **Mute Audio** silences the track as it would any other, and **Hide Video** doesn't.

## Adjustment clips

An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) on a track cut by a matte grades only inside the matte. This is how you confine a grade to one area: put the adjustment clip on a track, and make the track directly in front of it a matte.

An adjustment clip on a matte track does nothing. Its settings are kept, and the Clip tab says so.

## The note on the Clip tab

When every selected clip is on a matte track and those tracks share one mode, every sub-tab of the **Clip** tab shows a note under its strip. Every control stays live, and its value comes back into play when the track stops being a matte.

| Selection | Note |
| --- | --- |
| Clips on a matte track with a track behind it | "Matte for the track below (Alpha). Not drawn: its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect." The note names the track's mode. |
| Clips on a matte track with nothing to cut | "Nothing is behind this matte track, so it cuts nothing." |
| Adjustment clips on a matte track | "An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect." |

## On the timeline

A matte track's header carries a tag such as "Matte · Alpha", under the track name. With nothing to cut, the tag is dimmed and reads "Matte · nothing behind".

On a short row the tag shares the name's line, and it shortens to "Matte" when the name would lose its room.

The track's clips are drawn at half opacity with dashed outlines, and a bracket joins the track to the track it cuts. A matte that cuts nothing keeps its dashed outlines and has no bracket.

## Related

- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)
- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
- [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/)

---
title: Mattes inside nests
description: See what happens to a matte when you nest or un-nest its tracks, and when a transition crosses them.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) works inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) just as it does on the timeline. This page covers what happens where the two meet: a clip inside a nest, nesting and un-nesting matted tracks, and transitions across them.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Nest', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest']}
  keys={['⌘G', '⇧⌘G']}
  tools={['nest', 'unnest']}
/>

## Inside a nest

With a nest open, **Track ▸ Matte** works on the nest's own tracks, and a matte cuts the track directly behind it among them.

A nest clip can also sit on a matte track, or on a track a matte cuts, out on the timeline:

| Where the nest clip sits | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| On a matte track | Its whole picture is the matte, including any matte inside it. |
| On a track cut by a matte | Every layer it draws is cut. At a soft edge, overlapping layers inside the nest show through each other. |

For a clip inside a nest, Frame Job looks outward from the clip's own track through each nest it's inside. The first matte track it meets, directly or because the nest clip sits on one, makes the clip a matte. Nothing further out applies to it. Any matte it passes on the way cuts it, and those cuts multiply.

Two clips showing the same nest at the same moment each have their own matte.

## Nest

**Clip ▸ Nest** keeps a track's matte only when the track it cuts is nested with it. Select clips on both tracks and the pair carries into the nest, so the picture stays the same.

A matte nested without its target becomes an ordinary track inside the nest. Its clips draw there and the picture changes. Undo restores it.

The nest clip goes on the front-most of the nested clips' tracks that isn't a matte track, which is where a matte pair's picture was drawn. If every nested clip came from a matte track, it goes on the front-most of them, and the whole nest becomes a matte.

## Un-nest

**Clip ▸ Un-nest** lines the nest's front-most non-matte track up with the nest clip's track, so the picture comes back as it was. Matte tracks carried in the nest land on the tracks in front of it.

Un-nest never makes a track a matte. A carried matte clip is a matte again only if the track it lands on is one, as it is when you un-nest straight after nesting. With no track in front, or no room on it, the clip goes on a new ordinary track in front and draws as an ordinary clip.

## Transitions

Mattes work through transitions.

- A dissolve on one matted track stays exact under a soft matte, because both halves are cut by the same matte.
- A **Cross Dissolve** or **Zoom** with a nested half, or between clips inside a nest, mixes its two halves exactly, matte or not. Each half is drawn whole, with its shadows, reflections and mattes, and the two are then mixed. Layers inside a half don't show through each other part-way through.
- A matte inside a dissolving nest clip is drawn whole, and that half fades once.
- A nested **Zoom** half zooms as one picture about the nest clip's centre.
- Clips inside such a dissolve draw without [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/).

Push, slide, wipe and fade transitions aren't mixed this way. They apply to each layer on its own.

Mattes also hold through shadows, reflections, every [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/) and every export.

---
title: Backgrounds
description: Fill the space around your footage with a colour, a picture or a blurred copy of the clip, on a new track behind everything.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A screen recording that doesn't fill the frame, a phone clip on a landscape canvas or a title standing on nothing all leave the canvas showing. A background fills that space with a colour, a picture or a blurred copy of the clip itself.

To change the colour of the canvas itself, see [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={[
    'Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color',
    'Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image…',
    'Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background',
  ]}
  tools={['add_background', 'add_blurred_background']}
/>

## Solid Color

Choose **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color**. You don't need a selection, and there's no key for it.

Frame Job adds a canvas-sized white rectangle named "Background", starting at 0 and as long as the timeline. It's white because the canvas is black by default, and a black plate would seem to do nothing.

Recolour it in the **Fill** row of the **Shape** tab, or turn on **Gradient** there for a full-canvas ramp. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) and [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/).

## Image

<Steps>

1. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image…**. You don't need a selection, and there's no key for it.

2. Pick a picture. The panel offers any image type macOS can read, and only image files.

</Steps>

The picture goes behind everything, scaled to fill the canvas and as long as the timeline. It's named "Background". Fill means it covers the whole canvas and any overflow is cut off at the edges, whatever **Fit new clips to canvas** says. To see the whole picture instead, scale it down afterwards.

The picture joins the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) in the same undo step. If it's already there, the existing entry is reused.

If the file can't be read, an alert says so and nothing is added. "Could Not Add the Picture" means it couldn't join the project's media list.

## Blurred background

This is the usual backdrop for a screen recording or a vertical video: the clip's own picture, blown up past the frame and blurred, so the colours always match.

<Steps>

1. Select one clip.

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**. There's no key for it.

</Steps>

Frame Job puts a copy behind everything, named "Blurred Background", and selects the copy rather than the original, so you can adjust its blur or its scale straight away. The copy is:

- at the same start and length, with the same speed and the same part of the source, so both play the same frames
- scaled to fill the canvas, centred and uncropped
- blended **Normal**, whatever the original uses
- blurred by one full-strength Blur [filter](/effects/filters/), which replaces any filters on the original
- muted, so the sound doesn't play twice

The command works on video, image, still, shape and graphic clips. It's dimmed for a text clip, an adjustment clip and an audio-only clip, which have no picture size to scale to the canvas. It's also dimmed for a nest clip, because a blurred copy of a nest would come out sharp, and when you've selected no clips or more than one.

## What a blurred background follows

The copy matches the clip at the moment you add it. After that it's a separate clip: moving or trimming the original doesn't move or trim the copy.

| The copy leaves behind | So |
| --- | --- |
| Transition | It's alone on its track, with nothing to transition from. |
| Actions | A zoom on the foreground doesn't zoom the backdrop. A speed ramp is an action too, so a copy of a ramped clip plays at the clip's steady speed and doesn't stay in step with it. |
| Motion presets and Motion Blur | The backdrop stays still and draws sharp, before its blur. |
| Remove Background and Behind Subject | The backdrop stays whole. |
| Label and ducking | The label isn't copied, and the copy doesn't lower the rest of the mix. |

Everything else carries over, including opacity, rotation, corner radius, the colour controls, the drop shadow and the reflection. A rotated clip gives a rotated backdrop, and the fill is worked out as if the picture were square to the canvas, so a large rotation can leave the corners showing.

The copy's picture is always on, even if the original's is [turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).

## A new back-most track

Each of the three commands puts one clip on a new track behind every other track, and selects it. A new track is the only place that's sure to be behind everything, with no overlap to check.

The track gets the next numbered name, such as "Track 4". One undo step takes the clip and the track away again. The steps are called **Add Background** and **Add Blurred Background**.

## Good to know

- A plate is as long as the timeline when you add it, and it doesn't grow with the timeline. Drag its end to [trim](/editing/trimming/) it longer.
- On an empty timeline, a plate is one frame long.
- Fill stops at a scale of 1000%, so a source less than a tenth of the canvas's width or height can't reach the edges.
- With a nest open, a background goes on the nest's own tracks, behind everything inside the nest.
- A project holds up to 64 tracks, counting the tracks inside nests, and Frame Job won't add a background past that.

## With an agent

An agent can do two things the menu can't. It can paint the plate in a chosen colour and give it a length of its own, and it can use a movie that's already in the project instead of a picture. A movie plate keeps its sound and stops where its file ends, so only a picture or a colour runs the whole timeline. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).

## Related

- [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/)
- [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/)
- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)

---
title: Matte tracks
description: Make one track cut the track behind it, so text, a shape or a movie becomes a window onto your footage.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A matte track cuts the track directly behind it. Its own clips are never drawn. Instead, what they show decides where the track behind can be seen, which turns a title or a shape into a window onto your footage.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Track ▸ Matte"
  where="Right-click a track's header or the empty part of its lane ▸ Matte"
  tools={['set_track', 'add_adjustment_clip']}
/>

<Shot
  name="10c-matte-track.window"
  alt="The editor with three tracks. The Window track carries a Matte · Alpha tag and its rectangle clip is drawn pale with a bracket joining it to the Video track below, so the preview shows the video only inside the rectangle, on a black canvas. The Stray track in front reads Matte · nothing behind. The inspector's Picture sub-tab opens with the note: Matte for the track below (Alpha). Not drawn: its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect."
/>

## What a matte does

Any clip that draws can be a matte: text, a shape, a graphic, an image, a movie or a nest.

A matte belongs to the track, not the clip. Move a clip off the track and it's an ordinary clip again, and move one on and it becomes part of the matte.

Only the track directly behind is cut, so tracks further back and the canvas show through the hole. Adding, moving or removing a track can change which track that is.

The cut applies to everything the clip behind draws. Its drop shadow follows the cut-out shape, and its reflection is cut where it lands. It all works in the preview, in rendered frames, at every [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/) and in every export.

## Setting a matte

<Steps>

1. Put the clips that will do the cutting on the track directly in front of the track you want to cut.

2. Select one of those clips, or right-click that track's header.

3. Choose a mode from **Track ▸ Matte**, or from the **Matte** submenu of the track's context menu.

</Steps>

**Track ▸ Matte** works on the track holding the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected. The context menu works on the track you clicked. Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click its header or the empty part of its lane to open it.

A checkmark shows the track's mode. Choosing the mode it already has beeps and makes no undo step. There's no key for a matte, and the undo step is called **Track Matte**.

## The modes

| Mode | The track behind shows where the matte clip is |
| --- | --- |
| **Off** | Not a matte. This is an ordinary track, and every track's default. |
| **Alpha** | Opaque |
| **Inverted Alpha** | Transparent |
| **Luma** | Bright |
| **Inverted Luma** | Dark |

Brightness is Rec. 709 luma, and transparent counts as black, so a half-transparent white counts as half bright.

Everything outside a matte clip's box is transparent. So while a matte clip is on the timeline, **Alpha** and **Luma** hide the track behind outside the clip, and **Inverted Alpha** and **Inverted Luma** show it there.

## Gaps

Where the matte track has no clip, the track behind shows uncut, whatever the mode.

A matte is read moment by moment and no clip is tied to another, so splitting, moving, deleting or pasting can't break a link between them.

## Turning a matte off

To turn a cut off for a while, use **Hide Video** on the matte track, or [turn off a matte clip's picture](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/). Either way the track behind shows whole, as it does in a gap. To end the matte for good, choose **Off**.

## Nothing to cut

A matte with no target cuts nothing, and its clips still draw nothing. That happens on the back-most track, and on a track directly in front of another matte track. So two matte tracks in a row don't combine: only the one nearest the track behind cuts anything.

## Matte properties

A matte clip is drawn like any other clip, into the matte instead of onto the canvas, so most of its settings shape the cut:

- position, scale, rotation and crop
- corner radius and opacity
- colour, chroma key and filters
- spotlight and obscured regions
- motion presets and actions
- transitions between two matte clips

Animate the clip and the cut moves with it, so a moving title can wipe footage on.

A matte clip's blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect. They're kept, and apply again when the track stops being a matte.

**Motion Blur** has no effect either, on a matte clip or on a clip a matte is cutting. Both draw sharp.

A matte clip isn't drawn, but it's still there on the canvas. Click inside its box to select it, and drag it like any clip.

## Sound

A matte clip's sound still plays. A matte only changes the picture, so **Mute Audio** silences the track as it would any other, and **Hide Video** doesn't.

## Adjustment clips

An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) on a track cut by a matte grades only inside the matte. This is how you confine a grade to one area: put the adjustment clip on a track, and make the track directly in front of it a matte.

An adjustment clip on a matte track does nothing. Its settings are kept, and the Clip tab says so.

## The note on the Clip tab

When every selected clip is on a matte track and those tracks share one mode, every sub-tab of the **Clip** tab shows a note under its strip. Every control stays live, and its value comes back into play when the track stops being a matte.

| Selection | Note |
| --- | --- |
| Clips on a matte track with a track behind it | "Matte for the track below (Alpha). Not drawn: its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect." The note names the track's mode. |
| Clips on a matte track with nothing to cut | "Nothing is behind this matte track, so it cuts nothing." |
| Adjustment clips on a matte track | "An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect." |

## On the timeline

A matte track's header carries a tag such as "Matte · Alpha", under the track name. With nothing to cut, the tag is dimmed and reads "Matte · nothing behind".

On a short row the tag shares the name's line, and it shortens to "Matte" when the name would lose its room.

The track's clips are drawn at half opacity with dashed outlines, and a bracket joins the track to the track it cuts. A matte that cuts nothing keeps its dashed outlines and has no bracket.

## Related

- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)
- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
- [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/)
